page: Vultr vc2-4c-8gb is a Cloud Compute virtual server featuring 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the x86_64 processor includes 16 MB of L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AVX512F, and AES. The system is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage along with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates that this instance resides in the lower performance tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench register in the bottom 10% to 25% categories. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is average at 367.64 GB/sec, but drops to weak levels of 24.41 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks. Cryptographic, database, and compression operations, such as Redis SET and Passmark database tests, also fall into the lower percentiles, reflecting the shared nature of the CPU allocation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the vc2-4c-8gb offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads that require multi-core configurations and fast NVMe storage without demanding sustained high-performance compute. The shared CPU allocation introduces potential resource contention, making it less suitable for production databases or heavy computational tasks. It is best suited for development environments, staging servers, lightweight static web serving, and low-traffic applications.
